title: What Actually Is a Website Cookie?
sources: MDN, 'Using HTTP cookies' (developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/Cookies): a cookie is a small piece of data a server sends to the browser; the browser stores it and sends it back to the same server with later requests; used for session management such as sign-in status and shopping cart contents; often holds a session ID

Wikipedia, 'HTTP cookie' (History): Lou Montulli at Netscape had the idea in June 1994 while Netscape built an e-commerce application for MCI; cookies solved reliably implementing a virtual shopping cart; Mosaic Netscape 0.9beta (Oct 1994) supported cookies

MDN and Wikipedia, third-party cookies: an advertiser's cookie sent from many sites lets it build a profile of a user's browsing across sites (the basis of retargeted ads); Safari, Firefox and Brave block third-party cookies by default

lines.text: What actually is a cookie on a website?
that a website asks your browser to keep.
Inside, there's usually just a short ID number,
and every time you come back,
your browser hands that ID right back to the site.
That's how it remembers you're logged in,
or what's still sitting in your cart.
Cookies were born in nineteen ninety-four at Netscape,
to help an online store remember your cart.
But here's the twist: some cookies belong to ad companies,
and they follow you from site to site.
That's why those shoes you looked at chase you everywhere.
